title: Postmortem Witness contract
description: FROZEN. The single contract between backend (Chiraanth) and frontend (Disha). Do not modify without agreement from both owners.

EventType.description: action: something a human did or is doing. hypothesis: a proposed cause. status_change: a hypothesis moving between states. thread: an open question or loose end nobody has closed. resolution: an explicit spoken declaration that the incident is resolved; it is a statement about the incident, not about any one hypothesis, so it carries no hypothesis_id. noise: everything else, which is most of a bridge call. speaker_amended: the ASR retroactively reassigned the speaker of an earlier turn; shown to the user, never hidden.

event_id.description: Stable identity, and the ONLY unique key on an event. An event may be re-emitted with the same event_id when it is corrected — most often after a speaker revision. Upsert on this key, do not append blindly. As of 1.3.0 one utterance can produce several events, so (connection_epoch, turn_order) is no longer unique per event and must not be used as a list key.

connection_epoch.description: Which ASR connection this event came from. Starts at 0 and increments on every reconnect. turn_order is assigned by the server and restarts at 0 on each new connection, so turn_order alone is ambiguous across a reconnect. The join key is always the composite (connection_epoch, turn_order) - never bare turn_order.

turn_order.description: The ASR turn this event was derived from, as numbered by the server. Only unique within one connection_epoch. Always pair it with connection_epoch; see that field. Since 1.3.0 the pair identifies a turn, not an event: one utterance may yield a status_change and an action together, and every event from that utterance shares the pair. It remains the join key for speaker amendments - all events sharing the pair are amended together - but the unique key is event_id.

speaker_label.description: Diarization label from the ASR, e.g. 'A'. Always a label, never a name. May be corrected after first emission by a speaker revision.

speaker_name.description: Human name for the speaker, once known. Always null for now — populated later by a roll-call pass that maps labels to names. Render the name when present and fall back to the label when not.

timestamp_ms.description: Milliseconds from the start of the incident audio, not wall clock.

text.description: Verbatim utterance. Never paraphrased. This is what gets quoted in the postmortem.

summary.description: Short normalized phrasing for the timeline UI, e.g. 'Rolled back deploy 4c21f'.

hypothesis_id.description: Null except on hypothesis events (where it names the hypothesis being raised) and status_change events (where it names the hypothesis being changed). Required to be non-null for status_change.

new_state.description: Null except on status_change events. Never inferred: only set when a state change was explicitly spoken.

owner.description: Speaker who owns the action or thread, when one was named. Carries whatever was spoken — usually a name heard on the call, not a diarization label. Null when unowned.

confidence.description: Extractor confidence. The UI may dim or gate on low values.

previous_speaker_label.description: Null except on speaker_amended events, where it holds the label the turn used to be attributed to. Lets the UI show the correction as a correction ('A -> B') instead of silently swapping it.

text.description: Normalized statement of the proposed cause.

raised_by_label.description: Diarization label of whoever raised it. Subject to speaker revision.

implicit.description: True when this hypothesis was created by a status_change that named an id nobody had raised. False for every hypothesis that arrived as a hypothesis event. Must be present in both live diffs and a fresh IncidentState snapshot - a client that loads mid-call must see the same board as one that streamed from the start.

unowned.description: True when no spoken owner was given and the utterance was not a first-person commitment (so ownership could not be derived from speaker_label). The demo call embeds exactly one of these. Must be present in both live diffs and a fresh IncidentState snapshot.

DiffOpKind.description: One change the state machine emits over the WebSocket. The live board is updated by applying these in order; a client that missed the stream loads IncidentState instead. The two views must be equivalent.

SpeakerChange.description: One timeline event whose speaker_label moved during a SpeakerRevision batch.

OwnerChange.description: A first-person action whose owner was recomputed after its speaker_label moved. Spoken names are never rewritten.

ReconciliationSummary.description: What one SpeakerRevision batch changed on the board. Emitted once at teardown as a DiffOp with op=reconciliation. The live board ran on provisional labels; this is the correction.

DiffOp.description: One board change. Upserts carry a key; set_resolved, set_latency and reconciliation do not.

key.description: Map key for upsert_* ops (hypothesis_id, thread_id, action_id, or event_id). Null for set_resolved, set_latency, and reconciliation.

value.description: Payload whose shape depends on op: Hypothesis, Thread, Action, Event, boolean (set_resolved), Latency, or ReconciliationSummary.

StateDiff.description: A batch of DiffOps for the WebSocket. Apply in order. Never send a full IncidentState over the live channel - a client that reconnects mid-call loads IncidentState once, then resumes on diffs. snapshot() and the accumulation of every DiffOp from the start of the incident must produce identical boards.

Latency.description: Rolling p50 values in milliseconds, surfaced live in the dashboard.
